propositions: Recovery preflight refuses contexts over a flat 100k-char bound even when their product with criteria count (recovery input size) is under the previously ratified 3.2M-char worst case, causing live tickets like c9f7 (121k chars) to be unrecoverable despite fitting within economic limits.

The flat per-context bound conflates two independent ceilings: physical (single evidence run must fit verifier model window) and economic (recovery multiplies context by criteria count); the bound must derive from model capacity and actual product constraints separately.

The physical ceiling should be derived from the resolved verifier model's own context window via MODEL_LADDER lookup (not escalation max), moved from plan_review/sizing.py to shared model_classes.py; the economic ceiling should be an explicit product limit (3.2M chars) checked before any runner calls.

An unknown or unmapped model should conservatively default to the ladder minimum window size to avoid over-admitting context mid-run, with diagnostics {context_chars, context_char_limit, criteria_total, recovery_input_chars, recovery_input_char_limit} remaining visible on refusal.

The append-only store and test pinning prevent retries from ever succeeding once context is refused, so the bound must be right-sized on first validation to avoid operator entrapment requiring --force-close.

Refusal remains elision-free (full context reaches model byte-identical), the criteria budget (32k) stays <= derived context budget, and over-budget payloads refuse with zero billable calls, preserving all d59e pinned invariants.
